pr_title: fix(rust,python): handle edge-case with string-literal replacement when the replace value looks like a capture group
pr_body:
Closes #6755.

Addresses edge-case with literal string replacement when using the regex engine. If the replacement pattern looks like (or contains) a capture group string you could get some unexpected/failed substitutions...

## Example
```python
import polars as pl
s = pl.Series( "srs", ["."] )
s.str.replace_all( ".", "$0", literal=True )[0]
```
**Before**: `'.'` _(applied capture group, despite "literal=True")_
**After**: `'$0'` _(capture group syntax ignored, literal properly replaced)_

## Also

* Added test coverage for replacement patterns of this type.
* Making explicit use of `NoExpand` for literal replacement should also be marginally faster in general, as no capture groups have to be searched for at all:
  * https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/struct.NoExpand.html

issue_context.title: `str.replace` and `str.replace_all` cannot replace with the literal string "$0" when `literal=True`. (but only in some cases)
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

Replacing some strings with `$0` will replace it with itself, even when `literal=True`. When replacing with `$1` it will replace with empty string.

It's obviously taking the match groups.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

# . is replaced with itself
print(pl.Series(["."]).str.replace(".", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> "."

# . is replaced with literal $0
print(pl.Series(["1"]).str.replace("1", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> "$0"

# replace_all always replaces with itself
print(pl.Series(["."]).str.replace_all(".", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> "."
print(pl.Series([".."]).str.replace_all(".", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> ".."
print(pl.Series(["a"]).str.replace_all("a", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> "a"
print(pl.Series(["aa"]).str.replace_all("a", "$0", literal=True)[0])  # -> "aa"
print(pl.Series(["aa"]).str.replace_all("a", "$1", literal=True)[0])  # -> ""


def replace(pattern, replace):
    return pl.Series([pattern]).str.replace(pattern, replace, literal=True)[0]


# Happens with single chars that are symbols
replace(".", "$0")  # "."
replace(";", "$0")  # ";"
replace("[", "$0")  # "["
replace("]", "$0")  # "]"
replace("(", "$0")  # "("
replace(")", "$0")  # ")"
replace("^", "$0")  # "^"
replace("$", "$0")  # "$"

# Happens when just a single symbol is present in string
replace("a#b", "$0")  # "a#b"

# Empty string when using $1
replace(".", "$1")  # ""
replace(";", "$1")  # ""

# Other chars works fine
replace("1", "$0")  # "$0"
replace("ab", "$0")  # "$0"
replace("aa", "$0")  # "$0"
replace("1", "$1")  # "$1"
replace("a", "$1")  # "$1"
replace(" ", "$0")  # "$0"
```


### Expected behavior

When `literal=True` I would expect it to also replace with the literal string `$0`. I guess the documentation does actually say that the _pattern_ is taken as literal, but if the pattern is literal you have no reason to use match groups in `replace` (Since you know that `$0 == pattern` and `$n == ""`)

comments:
Looks like `val` needs to be wrapped with [regex::NoExpand](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/struct.Regex.html#examples-2) in `replace_literal` and `replace_literal_all`.

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/master/polars/polars-ops/src/chunked_array/strings/namespace.rs#L224

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/master/polars/polars-ops/src/chunked_array/strings/namespace.rs#L237

> Looks like `val` needs to be wrapped with [regex::NoExpand]

Yup; escaping `$ => $$` in the replacement expression works too, but `NoExpand` is definitely preferable as it will be slightly more performant (I'm literally making this update now ;)
@StefanBRas: nice find, and thanks for the report - fix will land shortly in `0.16.3` ;)

@alexander-beedie You're welcome and thanks for the quick fix!

I doubt I'd ever find it myself manually - it was only because I was trying out hypothesis for testing some expressions and `hypothesis.strategies.text()` produced the `$0`.

> it was only because I was trying out hypothesis for testing some expressions...

Good stuff; I'm a big fan of `hypothesis` - actively probing for edge-cases can really help strengthen the codebase.

review_comments: Why do we actually use regex when we replace literal? :thinking:

Speed; the regex engine was actually benching faster on longer strings - we currently use standard string replace only on strings <= 32 chars. See https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/4057 for all the relevant graphs.

(I'm sure I have the benchmark script around here somewhere; will dig it out and rerun against the latest code).
